clue.text: By the time that I leave my own work for entertainment

parts.note: come is used this way in phrases like 'come winter', meaning by the time winter arrives

indicators.note: the letter I leaving means it drops out of the do-it-yourself abbreviation

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work you do on your own home

explanation.surface: Someone explains that once they finish their own job, they will go off to be entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' takes the I out of DIY, leaving DY.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a funny play or show, a form of light entertainment.

clue.text: Perfect example of a Spoonerism from the turf accountant/policeman

indicators.note: a Spoonerism swaps sounds between two words, here the bookmaker and the officer

parts.note: a jocular British name for a bookmaker, a bookie
cop is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A clue boasting of a model Spoonerism built from a betting man and a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a strict Spoonerism: the syllables BOOK and COP trade places across 'bookie cop' to give COPY BOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook, as in 'a copybook landing', describes something done exactly by the rules, faultless.

clue.text: Two surpluses, too?

parts.note: more and over both mean in excess, a surplus
more and over both mean in excess, a surplus

explanation.surface: Asking whether two excesses also mean too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover and too both mean in addition, besides.

clue.text: 19 poster disparaging 19s?

parts.note: 19 is SPIRIT; someone against spirits, in the drinking sense, is teetotal or dry
an ad, advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A poster campaign against drinking spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is SPIRIT: the definition is a spirit of the woods, but in 'disparaging 19s' the spirits are alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek myth, a woodland spirit.

clue.text: Hot water carrier returns, never mind what the revelation

indicators.note: returns signals that the hot-plus-carrier pair is read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a pipe carries water
'any' means no matter which, as in 'any will do'

explanation.surface: A hot-water bottle comes back, and whatever the matter, there is a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns HPIPE into EPIPH. 'Hot water carrier' looks like one thing, a hot-water bottle, but it splits into H and PIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden insight or moment of revelation, as well as the Christian feast of Christ's manifestation.

clue.text: How to get 19-er beheaded? Puzzle given award

indicators.note: how to get suggests a recipe for making something by reworking these letters
beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: 19 is SPIRIT, so this is SPIRIT followed by ER

explanation.surface: Wondering how a decapitated ghost is produced, then a crossword is given a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes S from SPIRITER to give PIRITER, which 'How to get' rearranges with PUZZLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pulitzer Prize is the leading American award for journalism, literature and music.

clue.text: Traveller on the beat with little change from that using conventional fuel

indicators.note: with little change from means only one letter differs from the vehicle described

parts.note: a car running on petrol, a petrol car

explanation.surface: A police vehicle is barely different from an ordinary petrol-driven car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with little change from' swaps one letter: the E of PETROL becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol car is a police vehicle that travels round the officers' beat.

clue.text: A lot of fish right on the seabed?

definitions.note: describes where the answer lies, a thing rather than a place, hence the question mark

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the fish loses its last letters

parts.note: an anchovy is a small fish

explanation.surface: A whole shoal of fish lying right on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims VY from ANCHOVY. The definition is loose, flagged by '?': an anchor is what lies on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's anchor rests on the sea floor to hold the vessel in place.

clue.text: Scream with pain, not being brave

parts.note: to yell is to scream
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in pain, being a coward about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: Standard error illuminated setter — about a pound — the way actors appeal to voters

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a typo is a printing error
lit means lighted up, illuminated
the setter refers to himself as I
ca, short for circa, means about
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
a road is a way
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A list of a crossword-maker's woes and expenses, ending with the style in which performers win over an electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: A long charade of eight short pieces; 'a' and 'the' are link words. A PARTY POLITICAL BROADCAST is a British term for a short TV or radio slot given to a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a broadcast is a party's airtime pitch to win the electorate's support.

clue.text: See 9
Little man eating river bird following starter

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a pawn is the lowliest chess piece, a little man
a cock is a male bird
a tail is what follows behind

explanation.surface: A small man devouring a waterfowl after the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts R inside PAWN to give PRAWN. 'starter' looks like the opening of a race but is the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn cocktail is a classic British first course of prawns in a pink sauce.

clue.text: See 9
Translated, I fly, pursuing round moulding

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the Latin word comes after the round letter

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
volo is Latin for 'I fly', so the phrase in translation

explanation.surface: Someone translates 'I fly' while chasing a round piece of decorative moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' points to Latin: VOLO means I fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex architectural moulding, roughly a quarter-circle in section.

clue.text: Logical function for type of prison and judicial decision (do it with capital?)

parts.note: an open prison is one with minimal security
a sentence is a judge's decision; a written sentence also begins with a capital letter, hence the aside

explanation.surface: A puzzle about kinds of prison and court verdicts, wondering if capital punishment is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside plays on 'capital': capital punishment for the judicial sense, and a capital letter for the grammatical one.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic, an open sentence is a formula containing a free variable, acting as a propositional function.

clue.text: Bird of rubber in vulgar parlance

indicators.note: in vulgar parlance means as said in a common accent, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: sandpaper is something used for rubbing down a surface

explanation.surface: A bird named, crudely, after an eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: A broad Cockney or Australian accent makes 'sandpaper' sound like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper is a wading shore bird.

clue.text: Notes on ornament for the nose keeping it to the grindstone?

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the notes below, after the ornament

parts.note: a stud is a piece of jewellery worn in a pierced nose
IOUs are notes promising to pay

explanation.surface: Notes stuck to a nose stud while someone keeps their nose to the grindstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is the nose from the wordplay: keeping one's nose to the grindstone means working hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person applies themselves diligently, working hard at their books.

clue.text: Slander and briefly myths brought up as an afterthought

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: mud, as in mud-slinging, is slander
and shortened is 'n, as in rock 'n' roll
the Edda is a body of Old Norse myths

explanation.surface: Slander and some short myths raised as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses the whole run MUDNEDDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is something added at the end, such as an appendix to a book.

clue.text: Firm attachment to doctor with pain re-treated

indicators.note: treated means handled or processed, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm attaches itself to a doctor whose pain is being treated again.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-treated' looks like one word, but RE is fodder and 'treated' rearranges DOCTOR, PAIN and RE. 'attachment to' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An incorporated firm is a company formed as a legal corporation, so the word stands for the business itself.

clue.text: Suppress loud (music) in crossing

indicators.note: in places the loud letter within the crossing

parts.note: a stile is a crossing point over a fence or wall
f, forte, is the musical term for loud

explanation.surface: Muffle the loud music at the crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps for climbing over a field fence, common on British footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to smother or hold back, to suppress.

clue.text: One in climbing jaunts needs mettle

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the jaunts
in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: trips are jaunts, short journeys
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone on climbing excursions needs courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, and 'in' puts I inside to give SPIRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and mettle both mean courage and determination.

clue.text: Put in all you can to give to the dog

definitions.meaning: to fill up completely, as with a glass or tank
read as three words, '...', to hand something to a young dog

explanation.definitionFit: To top up is to fill something to the brim, while split up it means to a puppy.

clue.text: Taking in fodder, eking out critical situation

indicators.note: taking in means one piece holds another inside it
eking out suggests the letters are stretched out, so shuffled into a new order

parts.note: feed is fodder for animals

explanation.surface: A farmer feeds the animals while making supplies last, in a precarious spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EKING into KNIGE. 'fodder' looks like part of the farm picture but is a synonym piece, and 'eking out' reads as one phrase though it splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a knife-edge means being in a tense, finely balanced state where things could go either way.

clue.text: Try without head, yours having nothing in it

indicators.note: without head means the front of the word is cut off

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Y is short for yours, as in a letter sign-off

explanation.surface: Try it without your head, and yours will be quite vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without head' cuts ATT from ATTEMPT, leaving EMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty means containing nothing.

clue.text: If challenged, put back on the hearth

indicators.note: challenged suggests the word is turned around on itself, its two letters swapped

parts.note: to replace something is to put it back

explanation.surface: Told off, someone puts something back by the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'challenged' turns IF into FI. The hearth looks like part of the scene but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace is the recess for a fire, the hearth itself.

clue.text: Outstanding and too conscious of it?

definitions.meaning: standing out from a surface, projecting
excessively aware of being outstanding, that is, conceited

explanation.definitionFit: Proud means projecting slightly above a surface and also self-satisfied or arrogant.

clue.text: On what can be obtained from the net I depend altogether

indicators.note: what can be got out of the word suggests rearranging its letters

parts.note: to rely is to depend

explanation.surface: A gambler says he depends completely on whatever can be won from the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what can be obtained from' rearranges NET into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely and altogether both mean completely, wholly.

clue.text: Pain with everything? Apply plaster

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'
the sum is the whole amount, everything

explanation.surface: Someone in pain over everything is told to put on a plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apply' is part of the surface's medical advice; 'plaster' alone defines, a sticking plaster in the surface but plaster of Paris here.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is the mineral from which plaster of Paris is made.
